facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus
who worked as a butcher and occasional hunter and had contact with hares and rabbits
lesions on left hand evolving over 3 days
vesiculobullous lesions appeared on the dorsal aspect of his left hand and extended into the web space between the first and second fingers
the lesion extended to the palm and ventral aspect of the thumb with an eroded area on which pustules appeared
No fever or other systemic symptoms were present
Hemorrhagic bullous lesions on the dorsal aspect of left hand extending to web space between first and second fingers
Surface erosion with pustular lesions on palm and ventral aspect of thumb
Fungal culture was negative
bacterial culture showed Staphylococcus simulans
Polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae was negative
Initially hemorrhagic bullous lesions appeared

concepts.why: The presence of Staphylococcus simulans in the bacterial culture and the description of the lesions as hemorrhagic bullous with surface erosion and pustular lesions are consistent with a Staphylococcal skin infection.

The patient's contact with hares and rabbits and the presentation of lesions on the hand are consistent with Tularemia, although the negative PCR for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae and the presence of Staphylococcus simulans in the bacterial culture make this diagnosis less likely.

The patient's contact with hares and rabbits and the presentation of lesions on the hand are consistent with Erysipeloid, although the negative PCR for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae makes this diagnosis less likely.
The patient's contact with animals and the presentation of lesions on the hand are consistent with Cutaneous anthrax, although there is no clear evidence of exposure to anthrax spores.

The presentation of lesions on the hand with surface erosion and pustular lesions is consistent with Cellulitis, and the presence of Staphylococcus simulans in the bacterial culture supports this diagnosis.

The negative fungal culture and negative polymerase chain reaction analysis for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, along with the patient's contact with hares and rabbits, suggest an alternative zoonotic infection such as Pasteurellosis.

rationales.F10: Presence of Staphylococcus simulans in bacterial culture strongly suggests a staphylococcal skin infection.
rationales.F11: Negative PCR result for Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae makes erysipeloid less likely.
